brief: A support assistant is halfway through a conversation about a double charge. Below are twelve things it currently holds or could read. Each belongs in exactly one of four memory tiers.

Sort each item by asking how long it should live, who wrote it and who may read it. Working context lasts one step, session memory lasts one conversation, long-term memory holds durable facts about one user, and shared knowledge serves everyone.

buckets.label: Working context
buckets.description: What is in the prompt for this model call. It lives for one step and is rebuilt every time within fixed section budgets.

buckets.label: Session memory
buckets.description: What belongs to this run or conversation, such as earlier turns, plans and summaries. It is dropped or archived when the session ends.

buckets.label: Long-term user memory
buckets.description: Durable facts about one user, scoped to that user in the store, each with its source and an expiry.

buckets.label: Shared knowledge
buckets.description: A curated corpus of documents that every user may read, retrieved in bounded chunks with source ids and timestamps.

items.text: Tool result from the last step: 3 open tickets for this customer.
items.explanation: The model needs this result for the very next decision, so it sits in the prompt now. If it matters later in the conversation, the session keeps a copy.

items.text: The user's latest message: why was I charged twice this month?
items.explanation: The current turn is the reason for this model call. It goes into working context in full, inside the history section's budget.

items.text: The JSON Schemas for the four tools this assistant may call.
items.explanation: Tool definitions are sent with every call, so they are part of working context. They rarely change, so they sit near the top where the prefix can be cached.

items.text: The order number 55102, which the user gave two turns ago.
items.explanation: It matters for this conversation only. Promoting it to long-term memory would store a one-off detail with no lasting value.

items.text: The plan written at the start of this run: check billing, then check refunds, then reply.
items.explanation: A plan belongs to one run. The orchestrator reads it back each step, and it has no use once the run ends.

items.text: A summary of the first ten turns of today's chat, made when the history section filled up.
items.explanation: Summarising old turns is how history evicts within its own budget. The summary describes this conversation, so it lives and dies with the session.

items.text: The user's preferred language is Spanish (confirmed 3 March).
items.explanation: A confirmed, durable preference about one user is exactly what long-term memory is for. The date and source travel with it.

items.text: The user asked to be contacted by email, never by phone (stated in chat on 12 May).
items.explanation: The user stated it directly and it should apply to future conversations. It is scoped to this user and records where it was learned.

items.text: The user relies on a screen reader and prefers short replies without tables (stated 20 April).
items.explanation: This durable need shapes every future reply to this user. It is stored under their user id and nobody else's sessions can read it.

items.text: Help centre article: card refunds take five to ten working days (updated May 2026).
items.explanation: Help articles apply to every user and are curated by their owners. The agent retrieves a chunk and cites its id, but never edits it.

items.text: Internal policy: refunds above $500 need a second approver.
items.explanation: A policy document is shared reference material, not a fact about one user. It is retrieved when relevant and cited like any other source.

items.text: Release notes for version 4.2 of the mobile app, describing the new billing screen.
items.explanation: Product documentation belongs in the shared corpus. Its timestamp lets the agent prefer it over notes for older versions.
